findings.text: Early init service that consumes an in-memory archive image and populates the initial filesystem, reporting success through a null return and failure through a diagnostic pointer while managing its own temporary workspace and link bookkeeping internally.

Paired reservation lifecycle for the initial RAM disk image: one routine validates and claims the physical extent and publishes virtual bounds, while a weakly linked companion releases a virtual range back to the allocator with poisoning and a label.

Public synchronisation gate that delays callers until background population of the initial filesystem has advanced past its recorded point, with a defensive early-call path that warns once and returns without blocking.

Root filesystem initialisation entry that schedules the population worker on a dedicated asynchronous domain, enables user-mode helper activity, and optionally blocks immediately when background operation is disabled.

Asynchronous worker that runs unpacking under the initial filesystem context, notifies the security layer once content is present, then either releases or publishes the source image, clears its bounds, and drains deferred file releases.

Archive interpreter organised as a small finite controller with about eight conditions covering start, accumulation, header handling, skipping, name handling, regular content, symbolic link handling, and reset, advanced iteratively until the active handler requests a stop.

Streaming layer repeatedly invokes the current handler while tracking remaining length and current position, and its outer flushing wrapper resynchronises on padding patterns while treating any other unexpected byte as a fatal archive error.

Top-level image walk distinguishes aligned uncompressed data, zero padding, and compressed payloads, resetting progress tracking before probing for a decompressor, invoking it with a flush callback and progress index, and rejecting unknown methods, bad signatures, or trailing garbage.

Reservation first clears stale virtual bounds, ignores an empty size, rounds the physical extent outward to page granularity, requires full containment in usable memory and absence of overlap with already claimed ranges, and disables the image on any violation.

Post-unpack disposition is governed by a retain flag settable through two early boot options; when clear the image pages are released unless overlap handling already reclaimed them, when set the image is exposed through a firmware binary attribute, and the bounds are always cleared afterwards.

Crash-kernel aware reclamation comes in two build variants; the active one detects overlap with the reserved crash region, zeroes the whole image, frees only the non-overlapping prefix and suffix, and signals that overlap was handled, while the alternate variant always reports no action.

When the supplied image is recognised as a legacy RAM disk rather than the expected archive, its bytes are preserved under /initrd.image with creation mode 0700, with incomplete transfers logged and open failures silently ignored.

Test helper record groups together archive header attributes such as identity, permissions, ownership, linkage, timestamps, sizes, device numbers, name length and checksum, alongside pointers to a filename and to payload bytes.
Unpack workspace comprises three contiguous scratch extents sized respectively for a fixed header, for a maximal link target with alignment slack plus terminator, and for a maximal aligned pathname.
The fixed header length for the portable archive format is 110 bytes.
Two six-character magic identifiers select checksum handling: 070701 causes any supplied checksum value to be ignored while 070702 requests validation against a payload byte sum.
Test archive construction pads both the header-plus-name prefix and the trailing payload to a four-byte boundary with zero bytes and includes the name terminator in length accounting.

Successful extraction restores object type, ownership, link count, and size-derived block accounting, and timestamp handling depends on configuration: either exact archive time is preserved or the observed time falls between sampling instants taken around unpacking.

Several malformations deterministically fail unpacking with an error indicator rather than silent acceptance, including missing name termination with poisoned tail, hexadecimal fields carrying language-style prefixes, incorrect checksums, decompressor failures, and stray bytes inside or after payloads.

Failed runs can leave partial filesystem state: a checksum failure retains the already created first object while the second remains absent, whereas an overlong pathname entry is skipped without error while a subsequent valid entry still appears.
Entries sharing minor device identity and inode number are coalesced into a single object with an elevated link count, with payload supplied by the final member of the group.

Access ordering relies on an asynchronous cookie and dedicated domain: scheduling records the cookie, waiters synchronise on its successor value, and a waiter arriving before any scheduling emits a one-time warning and returns to avoid deadlock.
Background unpacking defaults to enabled and can be switched through a boolean boot option; the scheduling entry consults this toggle to decide whether to block for completion immediately.
Bulk creation exercise uses 1000 generated entries with derived pathname sizing based on a fixed stem plus decimal counter width.
Payload offset can be steered to a chosen alignment by enlarging the filename field with padding, and the implementation correctly recovers file bytes from such widely spaced layouts.
Regular file payloads written through the archive are readable back byte-identical through the normal file interface before cleanup removes the entry.

Initialisation first unpacks the linked-in image and aborts on any diagnostic, then skips external image handling when no image bounds exist or forced mode is active, otherwise attempts external unpacking with distinct progress logging and conditional fallback preservation.
Archive termination marker TRAILER!!! is optional; hardlink bookkeeping is released even when the conventional terminator entry is absent.
